To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the performance of Bayesian retrievals is degraded by the high dimensionality of real satellite observations, and that this performance can be improved dramatically by reducing the dimensionality of observations prior to application of the retrieval algorithm.

(1) a conventional multichannel Bayesian retrieval algorithm applied to a synthetic dataset with 3 real channels yields poor performance, (2) the performance can be improved dramatically by reducing the number of channels to a single dimension, and (3) the single dimension can be obtained from the 3 real dimensions by a principal component analysis of a dependent dataset.

the performance of a Bayesian retrieval algorithm can be significantly improved by reducing the dimensionality of its observation space and that the dimensionality reduction can be accomplished by a two-stage principal components analysis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new algorithms for retrieving geophysical parameters from satellite observations.
a fundamental problem in Bayesian estimation theory, which is the problem of dimensionality reduction.
the question: “What is the minimum number of channels required to retrieve the precipitation signal from a given passive microwave sensor?” The answer, we suggest, is one.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dimensional reduction technique described is a valuable adjunct to Bayesian retrieval algorithms, especially for high dimensional data.
the conventional Bayesian algorithm is not suitable for use with real satellite sensors, and that the reduced-dimensional Bayesian algorithm is a promising alternative.
the dimensional reduction technique has the potential to improve multichannel retrieval performance significantly and should be seriously considered for future algorithm development.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the dimensionality of a multichannel Bayesian retrieval problem should be reduced to its lowest possible dimensionality consistent with the desired accuracy of the retrieved product, and that this dimensionality reduction should be carried out in a way that is consistent with the Bayesian approach.
the use of pseudochannels to reduce dimensionality in a Bayesian retrieval algorithm is an attractive alternative to the use of the full set of real channels.
a conventional multichannel Bayesian retrieval is not the best approach for the retrieval of precipitation from passive microwave satellite sensors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in general, the dimensionality of a Bayesian retrieval problem must not exceed that of the error covariance matrix.
the dimensionality of a retrieval problem should be reduced to the lowest possible level consistent with a reasonable estimate of the error covariance.

the dimensionality of real multichannel observations is likely to be a significant problem for Bayesian retrievals unless a suitable dimensional reduction scheme can be devised to extract a small number of pseudochannels from the original N channels.
